intro: Picture this: you check into a roomy studio with its own kitchenette, like a private condo, then after work or a shopping run you head up to the pool on floor 8 for a swim over the Si Racha skyline, and stroll across to grab a meal at Robinson or Pacific Park in five minutes — Citadines Grand Central Sri Racha is a hotel and serviced apartment under the Ascott group's Citadines brand, sitting right in the centre of Si Racha town, Si Racha District, Chonburi, on Surasak 1 Road · What most people bring up is the rooms that are spacious and very clean, many with a kitchenette including a microwave, plus the rooftop pool and gym on floor 8 and a breakfast with a Japanese-style menu that works for both one-night guests and long-stay monthly residents · It has 136 units from Studio to Two Bedroom, starting at about ฿1,049/night, scored 9.1 from 381 reviews on Trip.com, with a particularly high cleanliness score of 9.4

body.html: Overview and who it suits — to put it as simply as possible, Citadines Grand Central Sri Racha is a stay for people who want "a home-like serviced apartment in the middle of town" rather than a beachfront holiday resort like the ones in Bang Saen or Pattaya · It is a hotel and serviced apartment under the Citadines brand from The Ascott Limited, a brand known for kitchen-equipped rooms aimed at travellers who need to stay a while · Open since 2015, it is an 8-storey building at 99/9 Surasak 1 Road, Si Racha Sub-district, Si Racha District, Chonburi, right in the city's commercial heart · With 136 units, many of them with a kitchenette, and a concept built for both short and long monthly stays, real reviews agree that the people it suits best are those working or running errands around Laem Chabang, the industrial estates and the port — engineers, staff at foreign companies, especially the large Japanese community in Si Racha, and long-term residents who want a kitchen to cook in and full condo-style facilities · Another group that says it left an impression is families and couples who want a spacious, clean room and the use of the rooftop pool and gym, plus people coming to Si Racha on business who want a central place within walking distance of malls and restaurants · On the flip side, anyone set on sleeping right by the sea with the water in front of the property may feel this is more of a downtown building than a beachfront resort, and should look at stays around Bang Saen or Pattaya instead · In short, Citadines plays to "living comfortably, like home, in the middle of town" with clean rooms and facilities that genuinely work well, rather than selling the image of a resort where you can walk straight down to the beach

Location and getting around — this is one of Citadines' top selling points, because it sits right in the commercial heart of Si Racha on Surasak 1 Road, surrounded by malls, restaurants, convenience stores and markets · The highlight that reviews mention most often is that it is a 5-minute walk to Robinson Lifestyle Si Racha and Pacific Park Si Racha shopping centre, the town's two main malls sitting side by side, so eating and shopping barely require calling a car · It is also about 500 metres from Phyathai Sriracha Hospital, with several of Si Racha's Japanese and seafood restaurants within walking distance, plus the market and Ko Loi pier, the town's seaside landmark · For longer trips, the hotel is close to Laem Chabang port and the industrial estates, which is the main reason working travellers choose to stay here, and it is about a 30-minute drive to Pattaya · As for airports, it is about a 40–50 min drive from U-Tapao Airport (UTP) and about 80–90 min from Suvarnabhumi Airport (BKK) · One thing to say plainly is that, although it is central and within walking distance of the malls, getting to other spots in Chonburi or Pattaya is still easiest with your own car, since public transport in Si Racha is not as dense as in bigger cities. The upside is that the hotel offers free parking, though several reviews note the lot is fairly tight when the hotel is busy

"New room, very clean, more spacious than expected, with a kitchenette so you can cook for yourself — great for working around Laem Chabang on a long stay · Easy walk to Robinson and Pacific Park, no car needed, and breakfast even has a Japanese menu. The only downside is the parking lot is fairly tight."

Room types and decor — Citadines Grand Central Sri Racha has 136 units in total, split into several tiers to suit both one-night and long monthly stays · It starts with the Studio Deluxe at about 37 sqm, which, even as the entry-level room, is more spacious than the standard rooms at most hotels in the same area · Stepping up is the Studio Executive at about 44 sqm with more usable space · The one-bedroom tier is the One Bedroom Executive at about 57 sqm, with a living room separate from the bedroom · And the largest are the Two Bedroom Deluxe at about 65 sqm and Two Bedroom Executive at about 80 sqm, sleeping up to 4, ideal for families or groups who want plenty of room · What sets Citadines apart from a regular hotel is that many rooms have a kitchenette with a microwave, fridge and basic equipment, making it easy to cook simple meals and eat in like at home · The decor is a clean, easy-on-the-eye modern style in warm tones, and several reviews mention a slight Japanese feel that fits the Japanese guests who stay regularly · Most real reviews agree in praising that the rooms are new, very clean, spacious, with comfortable beds, and quiet, and cleanliness in particular — scoring as high as 9.4 on Trip.com — comes up again and again · Most rooms are city view, since the building sits in the middle of town, and not every room sees the sea, so if you want a more open view, ask for a high floor when you book

Facilities, pool and gym — the highlight people talk about at Citadines is the outdoor pool and gym on floor 8, the top floor of the building (rooftop) · Putting the pool up top gives it an open feel and a wide view over the Si Racha skyline, a popular spot where guests head up to swim and relax in the evening · Next to it is a well-equipped gym for anyone who wants to work out after work or before starting the day · There is also a sauna and jacuzzi for easing tired muscles, which long-stay workers especially like · A facility that makes long stays more comfortable is the shared coin-operated launderette (self-service), so you do not have to send laundry out every time, plus the hotel's dry-cleaning service · The basics for safety and convenience are all covered, including a 24-hour front desk, key-card building access, 24-hour CCTV, a business corner, free Wi-Fi everywhere and free parking · The building is also designed to be wheelchair accessible · To be honest, the pool here is a compact one geared toward casual swimming and relaxing rather than a large lap pool, but as a downtown serviced apartment it delivers a full and genuinely usable set of facilities

Food and dining — Citadines Grand Central Sri Racha has an in-house restaurant that mainly handles breakfast · Breakfast is served continental-style, and what sets it apart from others is that there is also a Japanese-style menu to choose from, fitting the Japanese guests who stay regularly in Si Racha, and a point many reviews mention fondly · To be honest, breakfast is where opinions split clearly into two camps — some reviews praise it as tasty with a Japanese menu to try, while others say the choices are not all that varied and the taste is middling compared with bigger hotels · A key advantage of staying here is that many rooms have a kitchenette, so long-stay guests can cook for themselves, which is cheap and handy for daily life · Combined with the central location within a five-minute walk of Robinson and Pacific Park — both of which have food courts, restaurants and supermarkets — many people mix cooking in the room, breakfast at the hotel, and walking out to try Si Racha's well-known Japanese and seafood restaurants · Overall, food is not the reason to come to Citadines to eat in-house, but it works as a supplement, and the location and in-room kitchen make up well for the limited dining choices at the hotel

Service — service is another point that draws fairly consistent praise in real reviews, scoring around 9.1 out of 10 on Trip.com · Many people say the staff are friendly, polite and helpful, especially the housekeeping that keeps things clean and responds quickly, which lines up with the unusually high cleanliness score · There are staff who can communicate in English to look after foreign guests working around Laem Chabang and the industrial estates, and who are used to caring for the Japanese guests who stay regularly · The 24-hour front desk, help with calling a car, and flexibility in looking after long-stay guests leave many guests feeling well cared for · But to be fair, some reviews note that the friendliness and speed of certain staff at certain times is not yet entirely consistent across the board and suggest improving on this point · Overall, service is still a strength here and one of the reasons the review scores sit so high

Real guest reviews (the good and the bad) — pulling from Trip.com, Booking.com and Tripadvisor, the picture is fairly consistent · On the praise side: the central Si Racha location a 5-minute walk from Robinson and Pacific Park, rooms that are new, very clean (cleanliness score 9.4) and spacious, many with a kitchenette ideal for long stays, comfortable beds, the rooftop pool and gym on floor 8 with city views, a sauna and jacuzzi to unwind, breakfast with a Japanese-style menu, convenience stores and restaurants within walking distance, and friendly staff · On the watch-out side: the thing mentioned most is the fairly tight parking lot, so sometimes you have to double-park when the hotel is full · Next is breakfast with choices that are not all that varied and a middling taste in some people's view, the friendliness of certain staff at certain times not being consistent, and the fact that this is a downtown building with city views, not a resort where you walk straight down to the beach, which some people wrongly expect · Most of these complaints are things you can manage by setting the right expectations and choosing your room rather than being big problems, since the overall score still sits high at 9.1 and the hotel remains a popular choice for workers and long-stay guests in Si Racha

"Impressed by the clean, spacious room and good bedding, easy walk to the malls with no car needed · The only downside is the parking lot is a bit tight — when it's busy you have to double-park. Next time, even if I drive, I'd still come back to stay because the location and room are such great value."

Price comparison and value — nightly rates start at about ฿1,049/night for a Studio Deluxe during promotions, and generally run around ฿1,300–฿2,000 for a studio on a typical weekday, while the larger one- to two-bedroom rooms climb to around ฿2,500 and up into the several thousands depending on size and timing · For long-stay guests, the hotel has monthly rates that are clearly better value than paying nightly, which is the Citadines brand's main selling point · What makes Citadines good value is that you get a spacious, new and very clean serviced apartment, many rooms with a kitchenette, plus a rooftop pool and gym, sauna and jacuzzi at a starting price that is not all that high, in the middle of town within walking distance of the two main malls · Compared with hotels of the same class in this area, most of which focus on just the bedroom and breakfast, Citadines offers more usable space, an in-room kitchen and facilities for relaxing · Compared with a luxury 5-star serviced apartment like Oakwood in the same town, Citadines is a smaller building with slightly fewer facilities, but it usually has the edge on a more accessible starting price and a closer walk to the malls · In short, if you value cleanliness, room space, an in-room kitchen and a walkable location to the malls on an affordable budget, every baht you pay is worth it, especially for workers around Laem Chabang and long-stay guests

What to know before booking — a few things help make the stay smoother · One, if an open view matters to you, ask for a high floor when you book, since most rooms are city view and the building is 8 storeys, with upper-floor rooms getting a wider view · Two, if you are driving yourself, allow for the fairly tight lot when the hotel is full and arrive early to secure a spot, or ask the hotel about backup parking · Three, if you plan a long stay, ask about monthly rates and pick a room with a kitchenette for value and the convenience of cooking for yourself · Four, if a very varied breakfast matters a lot to you, set your expectations accordingly, since the choices here lean simple with a Japanese menu as the highlight rather than a big buffet — the alternative is to walk over and eat at the nearby malls · Five, make the most of the rooftop pool and gym on floor 8 in the evening, and check the opening hours of the pool, gym and sauna in advance · Six, when there are events or activities around Laem Chabang and the industrial estates, rooms often fill up fast, so book ahead, compare prices across several platforms, and choose free cancellation if your plans are not yet set

Verdict — from all the real reviews, Citadines Grand Central Sri Racha is the stay that suits people who want a spacious, clean serviced apartment with a kitchenette in central Si Racha — equally good for workers around Laem Chabang, long-stay guests, families and Japanese guests who want a home-like feel · Rooms that are new, very clean and spacious, an in-room kitchenette, the rooftop pool and gym on floor 8, the sauna and jacuzzi, and the location a 5-minute walk from Robinson and Pacific Park make it good value among Si Racha's affordable serviced apartments · The friendly service and review scores as high as 9.1 from 381 reviews, especially the 9.4 cleanliness score, are why it is a popular choice for workers and long-stay guests in town · But you have to accept honestly that this is a downtown building with city views, not a resort where you walk straight down to the beach, the parking lot is fairly tight when full, and breakfast has choices that are not all that varied in some people's view · If you are looking for a seaside stay where you can walk straight into the water, this may not be the answer, and you should look at options around Bang Saen or Pattaya instead · But for a stay in central Si Racha with a kitchen, clean rooms, a rooftop pool and a home-like feel at an affordable price — Citadines Grand Central Sri Racha meets that need well, and that is why it has won over workers and long-stay guests in Si Racha for years

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Citadines Grand Central Sri Racha, Chonburi

faq.q: Where is Citadines Grand Central Sri Racha, and is it easy to get to?
faq.a: The hotel is at 99/9 Surasak 1 Road in central Si Racha, Chonburi · It is a 5-minute walk to both Robinson Lifestyle Si Racha and Pacific Park shopping centre, about 500 metres from Phyathai Sriracha Hospital · It is close to Ko Loi pier and the Laem Chabang area, about a 30-minute drive to Pattaya · It is about 40–50 min from U-Tapao Airport and about 80–90 min from Suvarnabhumi · You can walk to the malls, but reaching other spots is easiest with a car, and there is free parking (the lot is fairly tight)

faq.q: Does Citadines Sri Racha have in-room kitchens and suit long stays?
faq.a: Very much so · It is a serviced apartment under the Citadines brand where many rooms have a kitchenette with a microwave and fridge · It ranges from a 37 sqm Studio Deluxe to an 80 sqm Two Bedroom Executive · There are monthly rates and a shared coin-operated launderette for long-stay guests, ideal for workers around Laem Chabang and the industrial estates who need to stay a while with a kitchen to cook for themselves

faq.q: What is the starting price at Citadines Sri Racha, and what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start at about ฿1,049/night for a Studio Deluxe of about 37 sqm during promotions, and generally run around ฿1,300–฿2,000 on weekdays · There is a Studio Executive (~44 sqm), a One Bedroom Executive (~57 sqm) and Two Bedroom rooms (~65–80 sqm) for families · There are monthly rates for long stays · Rooms fill up fast during events around the industrial estates/Laem Chabang, so compare several platforms before booking

faq.q: Does Citadines Sri Racha have a pool and gym?
faq.a: Yes · There is an outdoor pool and gym on floor 8, the top floor of the building (rooftop), overlooking the Si Racha skyline · There is a sauna and jacuzzi to unwind, plus a shared coin-operated launderette · It is a compact pool geared toward casual swimming and relaxing rather than a large lap pool, but complete for a downtown serviced apartment

faq.q: Who does Citadines Sri Racha suit best?
faq.a: It suits people working or running errands around Laem Chabang and the industrial estates, long-stay guests, families, and Japanese guests who want a spacious, clean room with a kitchen in central Si Racha within walking distance of malls and restaurants · It is not for people set on sleeping right by the sea with the water in front of the property, since this is a downtown building with city views — for that, look at options around Bang Saen or Pattaya instead

faq.q: What are parking and breakfast like at Citadines Sri Racha?
faq.a: Most reviews praise the very clean, spacious rooms and friendly service · But some mention the fairly tight parking lot, with double-parking required when the hotel is full, and breakfast with choices that are not all that varied, even with a Japanese-style menu as the highlight · If you are driving yourself, it is best to arrive early or ask about backup parking, and if you want a varied breakfast you can walk over to eat at the nearby malls
